note: Official CBSE table prints the unit marks exactly as shown above. b* denotes concept-based questions such as tactile diagram, data interpretation or case-based study for visually impaired students. Theory is 70 marks and practical is separate 30 marks.
mistakes: Management of Sporting Events: mixing committee responsibilities or tournament procedures.
Children and Women in Sports: memorising terms without knowing the meaning, examples and relevant corrective/participation considerations.
Yoga: writing an asana name without its procedure, benefits and contraindications.
CWSN: confusing inclusion, classification and divisioning, or listing organisations without their roles.
Sports and Nutrition: mixing macro/micronutrients, sources and functions.
Test and Measurement: confusing test purpose, procedure, scoring and interpretation.
Physiology and Injuries: mixing injury classification, causes, prevention, first aid and management.
Biomechanics: applying Newton's laws, levers, equilibrium, friction and projectile concepts without a sports-specific example.
Psychology: confusing personality, motivation, aggression and psychological attributes.
Training: mixing training cycles with training methods and failing to distinguish the component being developed.
order: Start with Management of Sporting Events because it establishes tournament terminology and fixture procedures.
Study Children and Women in Sports, Yoga and CWSN using compact comparison tables for concepts, procedures and precautions.
Complete Sports and Nutrition and Test and Measurement with definitions plus calculation/procedure practice.
Study Physiology and Injuries before Biomechanics so the physiological and movement concepts are connected.
Finish Psychology and Training with definition-to-application examples.
Revise all ten units using short-answer recall followed by case/application questions.
Keep practical-file and practical-performance preparation separate from the 70-mark theory revision.
